Ellen — thanks for the details and the attachment. We can support a 72-hour transient uplift but there are a few commercial paths; I outline two clean options below with operational notes so your finance/legal can pick quickly.

Option A — Temporary headroom (fastest)- 72-hour headroom provisioned on your existing subscription; usage beyond committed headroom billed at a 1.6x overrun rate for that window (prorated per-minute).- No contract amendment required for <96-hour windows; invoice appears on next monthly bill with an overrun line item.- Pros: instant, low friction. Cons: higher per-token overrun rate.

Option B — Staged overrun settlement (preferred for predictability)- We provision a temporary uplift bucket for the 72-hour window and convert expected uplift to a short-term add-on (48–90 day billing term). Overrun beyond the uplift bucket is billed at a blended incremental rate (1.2x) and we apply a small volume discount if you commit to a minimum uplift amount.- Requires a one-page amendment (DocuSign). Invoices: uplift charge is invoiced immediately as a provisional charge; any true-up (overrun vs provisional) reconciled on the next invoice cycle.

Prelim numbers (ballpark) based on your projection attached:
- Option A: estimated uplift charge = $11,400 (ad-hoc overrun at 1.6x)
- Option B: provisional uplift deposit = $9,200; expected true-up delta range = -$1,000 to +$1,700 depending on actual consumption.

Operational items:
- We’ll enable a temporary soft-throttle at 95% of the uplift bucket so you don’t get sudden rate-limited errors.- Can enable real-time alerting in Redwood Console and a one-off traffic mirror to help you validate.

I’ll loop Ben and Laura for pricing/contract approval; if you’re comfortable with Option B we can send the amendment and DocuSign today.

Best,
